questions.question: What will be printed to the screen when this code runs?
questions.explanation_correct: Correct! The second assignment overwrites the first. When print(age) runs, age holds 25.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Incorrect. The second line `age = 25` replaces the old value `20`. The print statement outputs `25`.

questions.question: How many values can a single standard variable hold at the exact same moment?

options.text: Only 1 value (the newest value replaces any previous value)

questions.explanation_correct: Correct! A variable box holds exactly one value at a time. Assigning a new value discards the old one.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Incorrect. A variable is like a physical box that holds exactly one item at a time. The new value replaces the old one.

questions.question: Trace the values of `x` and `y`. What does the final line print?
questions.explanation_correct: Correct! When `y = x` executed, x was 10, so y received 10. Changing x to 20 later does not change y.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Incorrect. When `y = x` ran, y took the value inside x at that moment (10). Changing x afterwards does not retroactively change y.

questions.question: What does the following code display?

options.text: 0 on the first line, 50 on the second line
50 on the first line, 0 on the second line

questions.explanation_correct: Correct! The first print runs when score is 0. Then score updates to 50, so the second print displays 50.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Incorrect. Python executes top to bottom: Line 2 prints 0, Line 3 changes score to 50, Line 4 prints 50.
